_comment: NH redistricting events: drives data collection for the nh-elections project. GIS hierarchy: precinct (town / city ward / unincorporated place) > municipality > county. Each precinct will map to a date-keyed GIS table of district assignments; use each plan's effective date and first_election to key it. NH legislative, council and commissioner districts are built from whole towns/wards/places (no splits except congressional), and NH House plans include floterial (overlapping) districts, so one unit can belong to two House districts. City ward lines are set by city charter and state acts and can change between cycles. status values: used | vetoed | never_used | superseded | failed (died in legislature) | unknown (not yet researched). office values: us_house | nh_house | nh_senate | executive_council | county_commissioner | ward_boundaries | nh_house+nh_senate (see offices[]). superseded_by is a plan id, a list of plan ids (when a combined plan was replaced by separate plans), or null for current plans. status 'used' means the plan was used in at least one election; superseded_by shows what later replaced it. Plans with status vetoed, failed or never_used carry used_in_election=false: skip them for collection. Dates are ISO YYYY-MM-DD; null means unknown, and every null or doubtful field is named in that object's unconfirmed[] list.

events._comment: 1980 Census cycle. Legislature enacted US House, Executive Council and NH House plans. Gov. Gallen vetoed the Senate plan (SB 1); NH Supreme Court retained jurisdiction (Monier v. Gallen) and approved a negotiated Senate plan before the June 1982 filing period; the Legislature then codified the identical plan as SB 25 (Ch. 45), passed by the House 1982-06-24. Session-law signing dates for 1982 were not found online; chapter numbers come from the RSA 662 source notes and the 1981-82 House/Senate journal indexes. Several 1982 city ward-line bills (Nashua, Keene, Concord, Dover/Manchester, Portsmouth omnibus) were vetoed and sustained, so 1982 ward geometry did not change in those cities via those bills.
events.label: 1982 redistricting (1980 Census)

election_dates._comment: Primary 1982-09-14 confirmed in Monier v. Gallen; general date computed (first Tuesday after first Monday in November).

plans.citation: Laws 1982, 29:1 (RSA 662:5); upheld in Boyer v. Gardner, 540 F. Supp. 624 (D.N.H. 1982)

plans._comment: HB 31 'establishing ward lines for the city of Berlin' (original title also re-districted Berlin's House seats). Ch. 43 amended RSA 662:5. Enrolled late in the session (around June 1982); whether it applied to the 1982 election is unconfirmed. Relevant to Berlin ward GIS.

Court said (May 21, 1982) it would issue orders on/after May 28, 1982 unless a plan became law. Senate journal (21 June 1982) states SB 25 is 'an exact duplicate of what has been approved by the Supreme Court'. SB 25 passed Senate June 21 and House June 24, 1982 (legislative-day dates), Ch. 45. Date of the court's approval order and governor's signature on Ch. 45 not found.
plans.citation: Monier v. Gallen, 122 N.H. 474 (1982) (court-approved plan); codified as Laws 1982, 45:1 (RSA 662:3)

events._comment: 2000 Census cycle. Gov. Shaheen vetoed the legislature's Senate (SB 1) and House (HB 420) plans; the NH Supreme Court drew both. The court plans were used in 2002: both were precleared on 2002-09-05, before the 2002-09-10 primary, and the 2004 legislature replaced them. Use is inferred from the court orders, preclearance and later history; I did not check the 2002 SOS results district by district.
events.label: 2002 redistricting (2000 Census)

events._comment: 2010 Census cycle. All plans enacted by statute. HB 592 was vetoed and the veto was overridden, so it became law and was used. HB 1671, a congressional bill, died on the table. NH House districts follow the 2006 constitutional amendment (Pt. 2 Art. 11) giving qualifying towns or wards their own district; I did not check the amendment against a primary source.
events.label: 2012 redistricting (2010 Census)

election_dates._comment: Computed: second Tuesday in September; general per federal rule.

events._comment: 2020 Census cycle. The legislature passed congressional plans HB 52 and SB 200; Gov. Sununu vetoed both, and the NH Supreme Court adopted a least-change congressional map. Challenges to the Senate map (Brown v. Scanlan, 2023-11-29) and the House map (City of Dover v. Scanlan, 2025-06-04) failed, so no lines changed. In 2023, HB 75 (Ch. 177) moved Strafford County commissioners from at-large to districts, first used in 2024. The 2025-26 push for a mid-decade congressional map failed (HB 1300 became a tax-cap law).
events.label: 2022 redistricting (2020 Census) and later changes

election_dates._comment: Computed: second Tuesday in September; general per federal rule. The 2024 dates apply only to the Strafford commissioner change.
